title: CPU pressure
summary: A double-booking audit report with a bounded plan problem: the overlap test wraps both date columns in DATEDIFF, so each execution compares every pair of a provider's appointments instead of seeking ix_appointments_provider. Concurrent sessions run it back to back. The healthy variant asks the same question with a range on scheduled_start and seeks the index, for a before-and-after comparison.

concurrency.description: Sessions running the report; one per vCPU saturates the target.

intensity.description: Providers covered per execution: 4 per level, so 20 at the default.

notes.T4: The PostgreSQL report hashes every pair of ten providers' appointments; two sessions hold the Burstable server's one vCore at its ceiling, and its CPU credits (cpu_credits_remaining) drain toward the 20% baseline.

variant.description: problem: the non-SARGable DATEDIFF version. healthy: the indexed range version (the 'after').

expectedHubSignals.signal: An expensive-query or CPU finding for the target
expectedHubSignals.note: Preview; coverage by target is undocumented (ADR 0013).

expectedHubSignals.signal: T4: CPU (cpu_percent) at 100%, CPU Credits Remaining (cpu_credits_remaining) falling
expectedHubSignals.note: Hub's PostgreSQL dashboard shows CPU; the credits are an Azure Monitor metric (Burstable tier).

expectedSymptoms: Sustained high CPU from a few sessions running the same report
The report's plan scans and hash-joins care.appointments to itself; each execution takes about a second
Switching to variant=healthy cuts CPU per execution by well over an order of magnitude
queryLevelEvidence: Query Store: the problem query at the top of total CPU; the healthy query beside it for comparison
The execution plan shows a hash join on provider_id with a residual DATEDIFF predicate
reset: Read-only; nothing to undo. Stopping the run returns CPU to the baseline.
